entries.title: Proverbs 9:1
segments:
Her seven pillars; which adorn her palace and give it stability. 
 
They who listen to the wisdom of God, shall receive from her an abundance of all good things; but they who refuse to hear her voice, must perish in the greatness of their folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:2
segments: Killed her beasts--mingled her wine; that is, she has prepared a sumptuous feast.  Compare

entries.title: Proverbs 9:4
segments: The beginning of wisdom is to know our ignorance, and come to God for knowledge.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:7
segments:
vv 7-9. 
 
  He that reproveth a scorner--increase in learning; wisdom continues her address to men, reminding them that it is only the wise who will be benefited by her calls, while scorners and wicked men will reject them. This is not inconsistent with

, in which she addresses "the simple," and "him that wanteth understanding;" for such may be conscious of their ignorance, and this is the beginning of true wisdom. 
 
They who most need instruction are least ready to receive it; because they understand not their own folly, and therefore hate and despise reproof.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:9
segments: One of the blessed qualities of true wisdom is, that a little of it prepares men to seek and obtain more.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:10
segments:
The Holy; God. 
 
The foundation of all true wisdom is the knowledge and fear of God.  A wicked heart separates men from God, and keeps them in darkness and self-delusion.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:12
segments:
Wise for thyself--thou alone shalt bear it; in an emphatic sense. Though our wisdom and folly affect others, the principal harvest from them must be reaped by ourselves. 
 
Personal responsibility is always recognized in God's moral government. The counsels of the good cannot benefit us, nor the seductions of the wicked injure us, without our own free consent.  Our wisdom and folly are our own, and we must reap their fruits here and hereafter.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:13
segments: A foolish woman; the foolish woman described in the preceding chapters.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:15
segments: Right on their ways; who are attending to their lawful employments.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:17
segments:
Stolen waters--bread eaten in secret; unlawful pleasures. 
 
Unlawful pleasures promise much good, but their end is bitterness and death.

entries.title: Proverbs 9:18
segments: The dead are there; in her house.  Those who have entered it are as good as dead, because "none that go unto her return again, neither take they hold of the paths of life."
